name: A tick log that never goes back
brief:
A tick log stores message times in the order they arrive, and its times must never go backwards. Write the class `TickLog`. `bool add(long long t)` stores `t` and returns `true` when `t` is not earlier than the last stored time; an earlier time is refused, stores nothing and returns `false`. Equal times are allowed. `int size() const` is the number stored, and `long long span() const` is the last stored time less the first, or 0 with fewer than two.

Adding 10, 12, 12, 11 and 20 refuses only 11. Four times are stored, and the span is 20 - 10, so the answer is 10.
constraints: Times are whole numbers of milliseconds, may be negative, and may pass 2,147,483,647.
A log may be empty when `size` and `span` are read.
hint: Keep the first and last stored time and a count, or a vector of times. Compare a new time with the last one stored, not the first.

examples.note: Each add, then size() and span(): only 11 is refused.
7 is earlier than the last time, 9, so it is refused.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. A hidden helper adds each time to a fresh log, then reads `size()` and `span()`.
notes: The invariant is that stored times never decrease, and `add` is the only way in, so one check keeps it.
Checking against `back()` alone is enough because the stored times are already in order.
`front()` or `back()` on an empty vector is undefined, so `span` checks the size first.

planted.slip: Refuses a time equal to the last one.
Compares with the first time instead of the last.
Reads back() and front() of an empty log.
The times are stored in an int and wrap.
